surveyDefinition.title: Video Streaming Subscriptions — consumer survey (Middle East & Africa)
surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A business-to-consumer (B2C) market research questionnaire about Video Streaming Subscriptions. Every question asks about Video Streaming Subscriptions specifically — not the wider market, not adjacent categories, and not any named brand. It is designed to tell a client what buyers in Middle East & Africa actually do and want in this category.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in Middle East & Africa who buy or use Video Streaming Subscriptions for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Currently has an active paid subscription to at least one video streaming service (e.g., Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max, etc.); Primary decision-maker or co-decision-maker for household streaming subscriptions; Aged 18 or older; Able to complete an online survey in the relevant language. Excluded: Individuals who only use free ad-supported streaming (e.g., free tier of Pluto TV, YouTube without subscription); Businesses or institutions purchasing streaming for commercial use (e.g., bars, hotels, offices); Cable/satellite TV subscribers who do not also have a streaming subscription; Children under 18 (unless surveyed via parent proxy, which is out of scope for this consumer survey).
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Video streaming subscriptions are purchased by individual consumers and households for personal entertainment use. While some business plans exist, the dominant and defining market is consumer subscription services (e.g., Netflix, Disney+, Hulu).
respondentBehaviours: Streams video content at least weekly
Subscribes to one or more paid streaming services
Engages with original content and on-demand viewing
May churn or rotate subscriptions based on content library
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income — these define who was recruited, not what is measured, so they appear in the audience definition rather than as questions.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with video streaming subscriptions and their viewing context, then moves into the practical details of how they discover, sign up for, and pay for services, including the rotation and spend patterns. It then explores their preferences and expectations, emphasizing local content, flexible plans, and value. Finally, it assesses satisfaction, friction, and future intentions, including switching triggers and advocacy, all while being sensitive to the region's infrastructure and payment challenges.

Geographic scope is global, but survey feasibility may require country-specific sampling.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, which of the following best describes how you used a paid video streaming subscription?
options: I watched something on my own subscription
I watched something on someone else's subscription (e.g., family, friend)
I had access to a subscription but did not watch anything
I did not have access to any paid video streaming subscription

data.label: I watched something on my own subscription
I watched something on someone else's subscription (e.g., family, friend)
I had access to a subscription but did not watch anything
I did not have access to any paid video streaming subscription

questions.insight: Top response: I watched something on my own subscription (55.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Family planners and mobile-first professionals drive own-subscription usage; budget students and rural connectors often rely on shared access or none.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, which of the following best describes your main reason for having a paid video streaming subscription?
options: To watch exclusive and original content
For the convenience of watching anytime, anywhere
To watch live sports or events
To watch content in my own language
To stay connected to shows or movies from my home country

data.label: To watch exclusive and original content
For the convenience of watching anytime, anywhere
To watch live sports or events
To watch content in my own language
To stay connected to shows or movies from my home country

questions.insight: Top response: To watch exclusive and original content (28.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Exclusive content and convenience lead, but family and local language are strong due to family and religious personas.

questions.question: How much do you agree or disagree with the following statement? "My video streaming subscription is an essential part of my weekly entertainment."
questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat agree (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mixed sentiment; many see it as important but cost and infrastructure issues temper strong agreement.

questions.insight: Top response: Watching alone, just for myself (70.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mobile-first and student personas drive mobile and alone viewing; family personas drive co-viewing with kids.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, on how many days did you watch something on a video streaming subscription?

I did not watch any streaming in the last 30 days

questions.insight: Top response: Every day or almost every day (20+ days) (30.00%).

questions.question: In the last 30 days, which of the following people in your household have watched something on a video streaming subscription? Select all that apply.
options: No one in my household has watched in the last 30 days

data.label: No one in my household has watched in the last 30 days

questions.insight: Top response: Myself only (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Family-oriented personas increase multi-person viewing; singles and students often watch alone.

questions.question: Who in your household typically decides which video streaming subscriptions to keep or cancel?
options: I decide together with my partner or spouse
No one in particular — we just keep what we have

data.label: I decide together with my partner or spouse
No one in particular — we just keep what we have

questions.insight: Top response: I do (45.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Individual decision-making is common among mobile-first and students; joint decisions reflect family personas.

questions.question: Which of the following situations most recently prompted you to start a new video streaming subscription or add one to your current lineup?
options: A specific show or movie I wanted to watch was only available on that service
A free trial or promotional offer I couldn't pass up
A price increase or change to my current service made me look for alternatives
Friends or family recommended a service to me
A major live event or sports game I wanted to watch
I was tired of constantly switching between services and wanted to consolidate

data.label: A specific show or movie I wanted to watch was only available on that service
A free trial or promotional offer I couldn't pass up
A price increase or change to my current service made me look for alternatives
Friends or family recommended a service to me
A major live event or sports game I wanted to watch
I was tired of constantly switching between services and wanted to consolidate

questions.insight: Top response: A specific show or movie I wanted to watch was only available on that service (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Content-driven personas (Mobile-First Nairobi Professional, Budget-Conscious Student, Content Creator Aspirant) and Family Entertainment Planner drive the top option; free trials appeal to price-sensitive students and rural users; sports option lifted by Sports Fanatic.

questions.question: Before you decided on your most recent video streaming subscription, where did you learn about or compare your options? Select all that apply.
options: Streaming service websites or apps themselves
Word of mouth at work or school
I didn't compare options—I just picked one

data.label: Streaming service websites or apps themselves
Word of mouth at work or school
I didn't compare options—I just picked one

questions.insight: Top response: Recommendations from friends or family (34.00%).
questions.distributionNote: High social influence across family and student personas; social media ads strong among younger mobile-first users; comparison sites used by tech-savvy and diaspora.

questions.question: In the past 12 months, which of the following ways have you used to sign up for or pay for a video streaming subscription? Select all that apply.
options: Directly through the streaming service's own website or app
Through an app store (like Apple App Store or Google Play)
As part of a bundle with my internet or mobile phone provider
Through a third-party streaming aggregator or platform
With a prepaid gift card or subscription card from a retail store
Through a cable or satellite TV provider

data.label: Directly through the streaming service's own website or app
Through an app store (like Apple App Store or Google Play)
As part of a bundle with my internet or mobile phone provider
Through a third-party streaming aggregator or platform
With a prepaid gift card or subscription card from a retail store
Through a cable or satellite TV provider

questions.insight: Top response: Directly through the streaming service's own website or app (28.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mobile-first and budget personas (Nairobi Professional, Student, Rural Connector) drive app store and bundle usage; family and religious personas favor direct/bundle; prepaid cards appeal to those without credit cards.

questions.question: In the past 12 months, how often have you started or cancelled a video streaming subscription?
options: I haven't started or cancelled any in the past 12 months
Once or twice in the past 12 months

data.label: I haven't started or cancelled any in the past 12 months
Once or twice in the past 12 months

questions.insight: Top response: Once or twice in the past 12 months (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: High loyalty among family and religious personas keeps churn low; budget-conscious and content creators churn more frequently due to cost and promotional cycling.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, approximately how much did your household spend in total on all video streaming subscriptions?
questions.insight: Top response: $5 to under $10 (32.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Low income and price sensitivity push majority under $10; family plans and premium personas pull some into $10-20; luxury and expat segments account for higher tiers.

questions.question: Thinking about the video streaming subscription(s) you pay for, which of the following factors most influenced your choice? Select up to three.
options: Access to exclusive and original content
Ability to pay without a credit card (e.g., mobile money)

data.label: Access to exclusive and original content
Ability to pay without a credit card (e.g., mobile money)

questions.insight: Top response: Access to exclusive and original content (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Content exclusivity is top across all personas; mobile-only plans key for students and rural; local language support critical for religious and diaspora; payment flexibility important where credit cards are scarce.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, which of the following best describes how you decided to keep or renew your video streaming subscription(s)?
options: I keep them automatically without thinking about it
I review them only when I get a renewal notice
I actively compare options before each billing cycle
I reconsider only if the price changes or I face a problem
I don't really decide – someone else in my household handles it

data.label: I keep them automatically without thinking about it
I review them only when I get a renewal notice
I actively compare options before each billing cycle
I reconsider only if the price changes or I face a problem
I don't really decide – someone else in my household handles it

questions.insight: Top response: I keep them automatically without thinking about it (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Habitual renewal driven by family and religious personas; budget-conscious and tech-savvy actively compare; price-sensitive users reconsider on price changes; household decision-making common in family-centric personas.

questions.question: When you're browsing a streaming service, which of the following signals most strongly tells you that a show or movie is high quality?
options: It's featured prominently on the home screen
It has high ratings or reviews from other viewers
It's recommended by friends or family
It stars well-known actors or directors
It's an original production from the streaming service
It has won awards or been nominated for awards

data.label: It's featured prominently on the home screen
It has high ratings or reviews from other viewers
It's recommended by friends or family
It stars well-known actors or directors
It's an original production from the streaming service
It has won awards or been nominated for awards

questions.insight: Top response: It has high ratings or reviews from other viewers (28.00%).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the most important reason you would choose a mobile-only streaming plan over a standard plan?
options: It lets me watch on my phone without needing home internet
It includes offline downloads for when I'm away from a connection
It can be paid with mobile money instead of a credit card

data.label: It lets me watch on my phone without needing home internet
It includes offline downloads for when I'm away from a connection
It can be paid with mobile money instead of a credit card

questions.insight: Top response: It costs less each month (40.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Budget-conscious students, rural connectors, and mobile-first professionals prioritize cost and mobile flexibility. Payment flexibility is key for those without credit cards.

questions.question: Thinking about how you watch, which of the following best describes your preferred way to access a streaming subscription?
options: A single, all-in-one subscription that includes everything
A basic subscription that I can add extra channels or content packs to
A subscription that lets me rent or buy individual titles on demand

questions.insight: Top response: A single, all-in-one subscription that includes everything (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: All-in-one is popular among families and premium users; budget-conscious and students lean toward sharing or free ad-supported options. Add-on packs appeal to sports fans and diaspora.

questions.question: When choosing a video streaming subscription, how important is it that the service offers local and regional content in your preferred language?
questions.insight: Top response: Very important (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Religious guardians, diaspora, and rural connectors heavily weight local content. Tech-savvy and expats are less dependent on local language, but overall high importance due to regional mix.

questions.question: Which of the following would make you feel that a streaming service truly understands your culture and viewing preferences? Select all that apply.
options: Shows and movies made in my country or region
Subtitles or dubbing in my local language
Content that reflects my cultural or religious values
Local news, sports, or live events
Recommendations that feature local titles prominently

Subtitles or dubbing in my local language
Content that reflects my cultural or religious values
Local news, sports, or live events
Recommendations that feature local titles prominently

questions.insight: Top response: Shows and movies made in my country or region (70.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Religious guardians, diaspora, and rural connectors drive high selection of local content and language. Sports fans and family planners also value local live events.

questions.question: If you had to choose, which ONE of the following trade-offs would you be most willing to make to keep your monthly streaming costs down?

Lower picture quality (e.g., standard definition instead of HD)

None of the above – I would rather pay more than make any of these trade-offs

questions.insight: Top response: Watching ads or commercials (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Budget-conscious students and rural users are most willing to accept ads. Premium and sports fans are less willing to compromise, especially on live sports and quality.

questions.question: For a video streaming subscription that includes the content you want, which monthly price would you consider fair?
options: I would not pay for a streaming subscription

data.label: I would not pay for a streaming subscription

questions.insight: Top response: Less than $5 per month (35.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Low income and high price sensitivity dominate; budget-conscious and rural users anchor below $5. Gulf luxury and premium binge watchers accept higher prices, but they are a small share.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied are you with your current main video streaming subscription?
questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat satisfied (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mixed sentiment due to infrastructure and content gaps. Rural and budget users are more dissatisfied; diaspora and premium users are more satisfied but still note local content gaps.

questions.question: Compared with what you expected when you first signed up, how would you rate your current main video streaming subscription?
questions.insight: Top response: About as expected (38.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Mixed sentiment with high price sensitivity and infrastructure issues; Family planners and rural users lean negative due to cost and quality, while tech-savvy and luxury segments are more positive.

questions.question: Thinking about your main video streaming subscription, how satisfied are you with each of the following aspects?
questions.insight: Top response: Somewhat dissatisfied (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Dissatisfaction driven by cost, content gaps, and streaming quality; rural and budget personas weigh heavily on lower satisfaction, while premium personas are more satisfied.

questions.question: In the last 30 days, how often have you experienced buffering or poor streaming quality on your video streaming subscription?
questions.insight: Top response: Sometimes (3-5 times) (30.00%).
questions.distributionNote: Infrastructure challenges are widespread; rural, sports, and tech personas report frequent buffering, while some urban premium users have better experiences.

metadata.storyline_summary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with video streaming subscriptions and their viewing context, then moves into the practical details of how they discover, sign up for, and pay for services, including the rotation and spend patterns. It then explores their preferences and expectations, emphasizing local content, flexible plans, and value. Finally, it assesses satisfaction, friction, and future intentions, including switching triggers and advocacy, all while being sensitive to the region's infrastructure and payment challenges.
storyline_notes: Adapted the consumer_profile section to focus on viewing context and content needs rather than generic product usage, reflecting the on-demand nature of streaming.
In buying_behavior, added a beat on subscription cycle and rotation to capture the common practice of churning between services, which is more relevant than a typical repurchase cycle.
In preferences_expectations, emphasized local content and cultural credentials as a key beat, given the region's high demand for local and regional content.
In satisfaction_future_intent, included a beat on friction points that specifically addresses buffering, payment issues, and lack of local content, which are top pain points in the region.
Throughout, the beats avoid asking about age, income, or geography, and do not mention specific brands or competitors, per the rules.
metadata.classification_reason: Video streaming subscriptions are purchased by individual consumers and households for personal entertainment use. While some business plans exist, the dominant and defining market is consumer subscription services (e.g., Netflix, Disney+, Hulu).
